gemma_review.summary: The agent surface analysis reveals a risk score of 45, primarily driven by overly permissive filesystem access and insecure browser profile management within mcp.json. The configuration grants the agent access to home directory paths and utilizes a persistent browser profile, increasing the risk of session hijacking or unauthorized data exfiltration.
gemma_review.why_gemma_changed_the_call: Static scanning found browser profile reuse, filesystem access, and token names separately. Gemma connected those into one install posture: sandbox first, because browser session state plus local file access plus credentials can become session or credential exposure if installed globally.
agent_constraints: Do not install globally on first run.
Use a clean browser profile with no personal sessions or saved cookies.
Mount only the project directory needed for the workflow.
Pass token names by reference only; never expose real values to the model.
Require human approval before shell commands or package-runner installs.
Re-scan the final MCP config before writing it into a persistent agent profile.
top_risks: Browser profile reuse can expose logged-in sessions or cookies.
Filesystem access can exceed the project boundary if mounted too broadly.
Credential names such as GITHUB_TOKEN require scoped tokens and value redaction.
hardening_plan: Run the MCP in a disposable workspace first.
Review the final MCP config before saving it globally.
Approve shell commands one at a time until the tool is trusted.

proof_note: Saved public proof fixture from a successful Gemma 4 review path. Fresh scans remain live and may fall back if the provider rate-limits.
